full_judgment: 6. Mr. S.S. Halder, the learned Advocate appearing to support the impugned decree of the learned Subordinate judge does not dispute this proposition of law as to a sale held illegally, but he has submitted that the learned Subordinate judge himself did not, in fact, give much importance to the question of the alleged illegality of the sale since the learned Subordinate judge held that even if the sale were valid the plaintiffs' interest as under-tenure holders were not affected thereby. This leads to the question of annulment of the under-tenures of the touzi. Mr. B.B. Roy Chowdhury has referred to the certificate of possession dated 17.9.55 issued by the Collector on confirmation of the sale. Admittedly, possession delivered under this certificate is a symbolical possession since, in the touzi there were under-tenure holders who were in actual possession. Mr. B.B. Roy Chowdhury contends that symbolical possession from the Collector on confirmation of a sale amounted to actual possession and as such the defaulting proprietors stood dispossessed thereby and that they could not have filed the suit for mere title without praying for recovery of possession in support of this contention he has relied upon a decision of this Court in the case, Almaj Khatun Vs. Ejahar Mir, 8 DLR 82. In that case a suit was filed for having a revenue sale set aside by deposit of the government dues. Earlier the Collector .had refused to set aside the sale by accepting the said depot sit under the provision of section 37 (A) of the Sale Act. The suit was dismissed as It was found to have been hit by section 33 of the Sales Act in that the ground taken in the suit for setting aside the sale had not been declared and specified in an appeal to the Commissioner under section 2 of the Act, Villa of 1868. But in that case a passing reference was made to the question of the effect of a symbolical possession on confirmation of a sale and it was held "symbolical" possession obtained in a suit for ejectment in respect of a plot in the occupation of a tenant-judgment debtor is effective to terminate the possession of such tenant." We fall to understand how this observation in will help the appellant before us. Symbolical possession is a good as actual possession against a judgment debtor, and this principle of law was finally settled as far back as in 1917 by the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in a case reported in 23 CWN 37. But in the case before us the under-tenure holders were not judgment debtors so as to lose their actual p3ssession by a certificate of possession issued by the Collector on sale of the superior interest, the touzi. it Is true that when a sale for arrear of revenue is confirmed and a certificate of possession is issued to the purchaser, the certificate of possession amounts to actual possession against the defaulting proprietors But the defaulting properties tors before us were also the under tenure holders a separate class of tenants in Khas possession. The Collector's Certificate of possession did not terminate their possession automatically.
